p.i: satisfecisse. Si quid tamen dubii superfit alicujus animo, & absit calumniandi studium, ei satisfacere semper paratus ero per Dei gratiam, quandoquidem de doctrinæ hujus veritate firmiter persuasus sum. Quod si autem quis vel ipse, vel (uti Simoniæ sunt quorundam artes) aliorum operâ, per meum latus doctrinam hanc oppugnare vel suspectam reddere ausus fuerit, adeoque larvam sibi egregiè detractam velit; sciat nihil esse tàm absconditum aut in obscuro factū quod non sol sit aspecturus cum rubore & confusione eorum, qui malè

page.notes: The first word "satisfecisse." is a fragment carried over from the previous page. The printed "&" after "animo," and after "rubore" is a ligature sign (et/&) and is transcribed as &. The line "sol sit" is printed as such and has not been corrected. The page ends mid-sentence, so the paragraph continues on the next page.
